questions.q: The Dronacharya Award is given to
questions.e: The Dronacharya Award honours coaches for producing medal winners. The Arjuna Award honours sportspersons for outstanding performance.

questions.q: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in
questions.e: The UN headquarters stands in New York City. Geneva hosts many UN agencies such as WHO.

questions.q: The term 'love' is used in which sport to mean a score of zero?
questions.e: In tennis, 'love' means zero points. 'Birdie' is a golf term and 'googly' a cricket term.

questions.q: The Santosh Trophy is associated with which sport?
questions.e: The Santosh Trophy is the national football championship among Indian states and units.

questions.q: The headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) is at
questions.e: WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. FAO is in Rome and the IMF in Washington, D.C.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about important days
I. National Science Day on 28 February commemorates the discovery of the Raman Effect.
II. World Environment Day is observed on 5 July.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: C. V. Raman announced the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928. World Environment Day is on 5 June, not 5 July.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a principal organ of the United Nations?
questions.e: The six principal organs include the Trusteeship Council, ECOSOC and the ICJ. UNESCO is a specialised agency.

questions.q: Match the organisation with the city of its headquarters.
questions.e: IAEA is in Vienna, UNEP in Nairobi, UNHCR in Geneva and FAO in Rome.

questions.q: After Independence, who won India's first individual Olympic medal, a bronze in wrestling at the 1952 Helsinki Games?
questions.e: Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav won bronze in freestyle wrestling (bantamweight) at Helsinki in 1952.

questions.q: Match the trophy/cup with its sport.
questions.e: The Ryder Cup is golf, the Davis Cup tennis, the Uber Cup women's badminton and the Durand Cup football.
